rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, own lysimeter experiment (nine weighing lysimeters, FI/SDI/SSDI, winter wheat 2017-18). Q2: Table 1 and Section 4.2 report grain yield and biomass under flood, surface drip and subsurface drip (FI 4694.8, SSDI 4584.8, SDI 4428.0 kg/ha). Q4: Section 4.5/Figure 6 measure leaf gas exchange (net photosynthesis ~15% higher in drip treatments, lower transpiration in SSDI) and Table 2 reports soil water storage, i.e. intermediate variables between irrigation method and yield. Q7: Section 5.3 states from own SPAD/gas-exchange results that sufficient water must be provided during irrigation so as not to harm the photosynthetic machinery, i.e. a condition for maintaining yield under drip.
rows.notes: Direction caution: the study does NOT find a yield increase from drip relative to flood; flood had the highest grain yield (Table 1, letter groups differ), SSDI slightly lower and described as 'similar', SDI lowest. The review's generalisation that all studies report yield increases is not supported by this study's own data. Q4 and Q7 are borderline: gas exchange was measured on a single day; the 'sufficient water' condition is a short statement in the discussion. No dispersion statistics reported (means with LSD letters only). Single soil, crop, site, season; lysimeter scale only; no explicit limitations stated.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, own weighing-lysimeter experiment comparing FI, SDI and SSDI on winter wheat. Q2: Section 4.1 and Table 2 report that SSDI reduced seasonal ET to 220.96 mm versus 300.30 mm under flood (26% lower, ~80 mm saved) and 259.60 mm under surface drip (15% lower), with irrigation input of 120 mm versus 190 mm (FI); Table 3 shows highest crop and irrigation water productivity under SSDI.
rows.notes: Water saving measured by one method only (weighing lysimeter mass change feeding a water balance). Soil evaporation, the asserted mechanism, was not measured or partitioned; the authors attribute lower ET to reduced evaporation citing Evett and others and list partitioning as future work. Leaf transpiration from LI-COR on one day is a different measurement but does not independently establish seasonal water saving. One soil, one crop, one site, one season; extrapolation to 1.7 Mha in Section 5.4 is a projection, not a measured larger-scale result. No limitations of own result stated; no SD/SE/CI reported for ET or water balance (means with LSD letters only).

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2-3, own lysimeter experiment on winter wheat under FI, SDI and SSDI.
rows.notes: The study contains no data or observation on weeds or any pest; it reports ET, water balance, yield components, biomass, water productivity and leaf gas exchange under subsurface drip versus surface drip and flood irrigation. Weed control is not mentioned anywhere in the text, so there is no own evidence on the claimed effect.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Single-season (2017-18) lysimeter study at one station in the North China Plain with one wheat cultivar and one soil; all statistics are means with ANOVA/LSD letter groupings and no dispersion measures are reported in tables or text.
